translationRepairs: Judged by these precedents, Yilige's remonstrance was stern and commanding — nearly the bearing of the gentlemen of old.
Judged by these precedents, Yilage's remonstrance was stern and commanding — nearly the bearing of the gentlemen of old.
Chinese 夷臘葛 is the chapter subject Yilage (耶律夷臘葛); idiomatic's Yilige is a misspelling, and the proposed Yilage matches the rest of the chapter.
When the Zhou emperor Shizong returned north ill, Siwen withdrew to Yijin and pretended not to know where the enemy were.
When the Later Zhou emperor Chai Rong returned because of illness, Siwen withdrew to Yijin and pretended not to know where the enemy was.
周主榮 identifies the Later Zhou emperor Chai Rong; the source says he returned because of illness but does not say that he returned north.
